# Owned plan read contract

This is the first bounded new unit of the alternate development runner. It specifies `_read_owned(account, _SourceRole.PLAN)`. It grants no plan, stage, source, native, export, or provenance acceptance. The original 26 owners remain unchanged. The owned-read boundary is implemented and locally verified. The four-row runner remains at its test-first stage. Local component evidence supplies no native or merge authority.

## Caller and data

The future planner caller owns its output directory and its already-open directory descriptor. After the planner terminates, the caller passes its one `_AttemptAccount` to `_read_owned`. The result provides full bytes for later strict plan validation. The caller must still validate the canonical plan digest and content before another row. No constructor acquires a root, validates external context, or creates PreparedR.

`_SourceRole` has exactly one member, `PLAN`, whose internal relative name is `plan.json`. This is the actual planner `--plan-output` and executor `--plan` basename in the frozen original vectors. The file limit is 8 MiB. Its retained category is reports and identity, limited to 16 MiB. Other roles, XML parsing, source collection, streams, preparation, controls, and exports remain closed until separate specifications exist. No arbitrary path, runtime cap, callback, launcher, fault option, or role registry is accepted.

`_OwnedRoot` is frozen passive data containing an absolute normalized `Path`, borrowed directory descriptor, device, inode, owner UID, and full mode. The caller keeps that descriptor open throughout the call. `_AttemptAccount` contains that root, an absolute monotonic nanosecond deadline, an explicit immutable tuple of sensitive byte strings, and five mutable facts. Those facts are total `spent_bytes`, actual `read_bytes`, retained report `retained_bytes`, `retained_members`, and `metadata_visits`. `stopped` is a permanent failure flag. There is one mutable new account. The constructor performs no I/O and confers no authority.

`_FileIdentity` is frozen and contains device, inode, full mode, UID, GID, link count, size, modification nanoseconds, and change nanoseconds. `_CompleteOwnedRead` is frozen and contains role, immutable bytes, lowercase full SHA-256, and the equal before, opened, after, and current identities. It has no optional success fields. No untrusted path or exception text is returned.

## Shape and ownership

The boundary validates passive input before filesystem work. Require exact data types, excluding bool from every integer. All counters are nonnegative and no greater than their fixed cap. `read_bytes <= spent_bytes`. The descriptor is in [0, 2**31-1]. Deadline is in [1, 2**63-1]. Identity device and inode fit unsigned 64 bits, UID and mode unsigned 32 bits. Sensitive values form an exact tuple of at most 32 exact bytes objects, each 8 through 4096 bytes. The bounded caller supplies these values; this unit does not read environment secrets or prove completeness of the tuple. Unknown role, bad shape, expired clock, already stopped account, or missing platform open flags refuses before filesystem work. Refusal raises `_OwnedReadError` with a fixed reason and leaves acceptance stopped. A previously stopped account stays stopped.

The root is a private output directory, never the filesystem anchor. Its path has at most 4096 encoded bytes and 1 through 64 non-anchor components, with no dot or dot-dot component or lexical normalization discrepancy. Refuse an anchor-shaped path before any filesystem operation. Check every component using non-following metadata before and after the read. Every component is a directory, never a symlink. The root itself must have the recorded device, inode, UID and full mode, UID equal to the current process UID, and mode exactly directory plus 0700. The borrowed descriptor's metadata must agree with that root before and after. Ancestors need not be process-owned. Their directory kind and absence of symlinks are checked twice, without a hostile concurrent-rename guarantee.

The only child name is `plan.json`, inspected and opened relative to the borrowed root descriptor. This makes containment independent of string concatenation and prevents substitution through a parent symlink during open. The child must be a regular file owned by the process, with one link and no group or other permission bits. Owner read/write bits may vary. Its size is from 0 through 8 MiB. Its four identities must agree in every named field. File metadata must fit unsigned 64-bit device/inode/link/size, unsigned 32-bit mode/UID/GID, and signed 64-bit times before it can enter the result. No untrusted serialization occurs in this unit.

## Admission and debit

One MiB is 1048576 bytes. The new pool is fixed at 256 MiB. One MiB of that pool stays held for closure, including the 64 KiB footer. Ordinary reads cannot spend it. There is no cap override, cap loan, refund of performed work, reset, or retry after failure. Original 512 MiB and combined 768 MiB limits remain separate future join obligations. Their unused capacity never increases this account.

Metadata is a separate bounded operation count, not fictitious byte traversal. The new account admits at most 20000 metadata calls. For a root with depth d, reserve capacity for `2*d + 6` calls before the first metadata effect. Debit one visit immediately before each actual metadata attempt, including an attempt that raises. Before payload admission the only allowed metadata is d ancestor/root lstats, one root-descriptor fstat, and one child non-following stat, in that order. Thus a payload quota denial performs d+2 visits, opens no new descriptor, reads no payload, and leaves `spent_bytes` and `read_bytes` unchanged. Insufficient metadata capacity refuses before any metadata call. There is no directory enumeration.

After this metadata identifies size n, reserve payload work B = `(s + 4) * (n + 1)` bytes, where s is the number of supplied sensitive strings. Require `spent_bytes + B <= 256 MiB - 1 MiB`, `retained_bytes + n <= 16 MiB`, and `retained_members + 1 <= 64` before open. The extra byte admits overrun detection, including for an empty file. One member slot is an in-memory retained result, not a physical exported file. The 64 slots reserve room within the eventual outer 128-file limit when paired with the old 64-file allowance; actual export accounting still requires its later owner. A reference to this result incurs no second byte copy. Every subsequent successful call retains a new result and pays again.

Open with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, relative to the borrowed root descriptor. Only this new descriptor is owned by the call. Use one unbuffered `os.read(fd, n+1)` so all returned bytes are visible to accounting. A short return, extra byte, or any identity change refuses. The bound intentionally rejects a short regular-file syscall instead of silently returning truncated data. A complete read charges n actual read bytes, n SHA-256 input bytes, `(s+1)*n` sensitivity scan bytes, and n retained-copy bytes, for `(s+4)*n` spent bytes. The retained-copy charge is the filesystem payload copied into the immutable returned buffer, not an invented physical export file. The same n bytes also occupy the reports category; that category occupancy is not added again to spent bytes. No extra assembled copy or payload serialization is permitted without another admission and debit.

The sensitivity pass checks all supplied secrets and the original fixed token-pattern family, case-insensitively where the original pattern does so. The pattern is `authorization` followed by whitespace, colon, whitespace and `bearer `, or `github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]+`, or `gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]+`, or `X-Amz-Signature=`, or `sig=`. A match withholds the result and permanently stops acceptance. No bytes, digest, path, or exception detail is included in the refusal. Sensitivity here supplies no standalone public-release authority.

After payload admission, any failure conservatively spends all B bytes permanently. `read_bytes` still records the exact returned syscall byte count, including an extra byte. If the syscall raises without returning bytes, its observed count is zero; B still covers its uncertain work. Failed reads retain zero new members and zero new category bytes. Successful reads spend only performed `(s+4)*n`; unused admitted capacity is never posted as spent. Cleanup does not turn a failure into success. Fixed bounded error reasons require no user-object traversal, exception formatting, or raw diagnostics.

Close the owned file descriptor on every path after a successful open, including fstat, read, hash, sensitivity, clock, and close failure. Never close the borrowed root descriptor. A close error stops acceptance and charges B. Before open and each payload operation, and after the final checks and close, require current monotonic time strictly below the supplied deadline. Metadata operations also check that deadline individually. The function does not start or reset any clock. A caller must provide the existing live or once-started final clock; this unit cannot assert that the caller did so. A syscall can exceed a deadline before control returns. No hard kernel-time or hostile same-UID containment guarantee is claimed.

## Verification boundary

Paired tests use real private temporary directories, real descriptors, and tiny local bytes. A narrow `os.open` recorder delegates to the real syscall and proves that accepted reads open the file while denied reads do not. Narrow read wrappers may modify the actual file immediately before the real read to test truncation, growth, or stable-size mode change. Those are test faults, never runtime API options. Open-failure and short-return tests are explicitly synthetic syscall faults and earn no native execution credit.

Tests assert returned bytes, digest, identities, immutability, closure, exact debit, retention, and permanent stop. Exact admission below, at, and above B uses already-spent counters near the unchanged 256 MiB limit. All post-return assertions remain unexecuted before implementation. The only intended before failure is the exact `_read_owned` body raising `NotImplementedError('NEW owned-read boundary missing')`. Unexpected setup, import, or runtime exceptions propagate. Root independently reviews this SPEC and the tests before the first local run.

Whole actual integration, row transitions, finalization, Linux process lifetime, all source identities, complete sensitive-input gathering, old/new join, physical export bounds, XML validation, canonical plan acceptance, and genuine original15 execution remain unimplemented and uncredited. Small-file results do not prove whole-runtime fit. Rollback removes only this isolated candidate after root capture; the historical observer and original owner texts remain intact.


# Original four rows and direct child lifetime

Draft only, 27 October 2026 Europe/Berlin. This unit supplies literal vectors and bounded Linux direct-child facts for the future `_original15` caller. It supplies no canonical-product validation, PreparedR authority, genuine Git preparation, native acceptance, export or origin. All 26 original owners and the owned-read unit stay unchanged. This addendum is subordinate to `synthesis.md`, `row-lifecycle-proposal.md` and `root-five-corrections.json`. The method selection retires the old observer duties. No syscall observer is restored.

## Frozen call shape

`_OriginalStage` has exactly PLANNER, EXECUTOR, RECONCILER and BINDER, in that order. `_PreparedPaths(root, out, home, tmp)` is frozen passive Path data. It never asserts preparation or authenticity. The existing tool supplies python, site_packages, core_root, modules_root and uv. `_original_vectors(tool, prepared)` returns four frozen `_OriginalVector(stage, argv, environment, cwd, expected_exit, seconds)` values. argv is a tuple of bytes, environment a tuple of seven byte-key/value pairs, cwd bytes. No caller supplies argv, environment, caps, callbacks or fault policies.

`_run_original_stage(account, tool, prepared, timer, stage)` chooses exactly one of these vectors and owns its Linux direct child until cleanup and reap. It uses the existing `_AttemptAccount`; add only `row_seconds`, `stream_bytes`, `retained_stream_bytes`, and `last_direct`. These are actual elapsed row work, actual stream reads, retained stream bytes and the latest immutable direct result. They are not a second ledger or authority. Existing spent/read/metadata counters also pay this work; report retention remains distinct. No row-order state is added. The future `_original15` owns canonical acceptance between rows. Any failed row sets the existing permanent stopped flag, which forbids every later row.

`_DirectResult` is frozen. Its fields are stage, vector, pid (None only before registration), started, deadline, ended, waitid (None or exact si_pid/si_code/si_status triple), wait_status (None or the actual direct waitpid status), stdout, stderr, cleanup_complete, deadline_seen and reason. reason is one of `complete`, `prerequisite`, `launch`, `deadline`, `stream-limit`, `budget`, `ownership`, `proc`, `cleanup`, `exit`, `exception`. It contains no arbitrary exception text. All observations remain raw facts. `complete` means this one direct row matched its expected normal exit and sampled cleanup completed. It never means native proof. The account retains last_direct even on failure; a returned result is the same immutable object, not an extra payload copy. A controlled refusal raises `_OriginalStageError` carrying that result. Other exceptions, including non-Deadline handler errors, retain their original identity after cleanup; last_direct records bounded secondary facts. No exception becomes success.

The two named missing bodies are `NotImplementedError('NEW original vectors missing')` and `NotImplementedError('NEW original row lifetime missing')`. Scaffold imports and passive declarations must load normally. These exact missing-body failures, not import/setup errors, are the only planned before-implementation evidence.

## Exact vectors and clocks

The source of literal vectors is original `replay.py` lines 1169–1195 and original contract section 5, including both complete bootstrap strings. Tests independently spell all four tuples. Preserve C `9b5ad1e78430cc0b061cb16de42f73de96f4f312`, R `4ae6175a4d337296d0347e73b66c9da1f0e43f7f`, source label, all filenames/options, order, cwd R, shell false, and exactly seven requested environment keys. No `-B`, marker descriptor, ambient variable, import hook or alternative executor is added. Native argv remains unchanged when controlled synthetic fixture source occupies C/src or C/scripts in tests.

Paths are absolute normalized Path values, at most 4096 encoded bytes each, with no NUL or dot-dot. Reject bad paths before effects. This only makes literal substitution safe; later preparation owns containment and source authentication. No filesystem validation occurs in vector construction.

Expected normal exits are 0/1/0/0; ceilings are 120/660/120/120 seconds. At row entry record monotonic started and calculate deadline once as min(started + row ceiling, timer.end, started + (1020 - account.row_seconds)). Require the original live Timer callable and unchanged end; account.deadline_ns may only further shorten it, never extend it. Update row_seconds by actual monotonic execution elapsed until cleanup begins, including failed work. Execution never borrows cleanup grace. Original Timer1200 includes original setup and is never restarted. Original executor600/installer120/probe10 remain untouched. Tests use shorter original Timer durations for harmless controls; production receives the actual existing Timer1200.

## Linux ownership and signals

Use genuine Linux, one parent thread, SIGALRM unblocked, SIGCHLD default, no competing waiter. Establish outer finally before handler change or launch. A real harmless waitability child must produce repeated consistent WNOWAIT observations and then a consistent reap before any native row. Account no success on missing WNOWAIT, ECHILD or unavailable prerequisites. Its fixed source and costs belong to the reviewed closure. Its result is a prerequisite, never a native row. No ctypes, compiler or hidden signal flag query.

Save the actual bound `timer.alarm` callable and timer.end. The row adapter forwards the exact signal and frame to that saved callable and catches only Deadline into a sticky flag. New row code never assigns pending, expired or deferred, and never cancels or rearms the timer itself or suppresses another exception. The original Timer callable and Timer.check retain existing source semantics, including their own pending/expired mutations and cancellation. Test-only state-denial setup and teardown are not runtime permissions. Check captured Deadline, timer.pending, timer.expired, time >= end and timer.check at every safe point, especially registration, output/wait steps, cleanup entry, restoration and return. Deferred pending with no active alarm still refuses. Restore the exact saved callable in every exit path, after the last group operation and direct-reap attempt. Existing Timer sources and semantics stay intact.

Use subprocess.Popen with shell=False, close_fds=True, pass_fds=(), start_new_session=True, stdin=DEVNULL, stdout/stderr=PIPE. The fixed private preexec resets SIGALRM to SIG_DFL first, empties the signal mask, applies tighter existing limits, verifies its pid=pgrp=session >1 and checks the absolute deadline immediately before exec. Do not call inherited Timer code. Limits preserve any tighter soft or hard limit, cap CPU at240 seconds, address space2147483648 bytes, file size268435456 bytes, NPROC128, core0, without relaxing inherited hard limits. No credential bytes are inspected/exported from inherited memory. Fork-memory isolation is not claimed.

Keep Popen strongly owned. No poll/wait/communicate, context-manager reap or convenience signal method while group identity is needed. Observe terminal state through real waitid(P_PID,pid,WEXITED|WNOHANG|WNOWAIT). Preserve si_pid/code/status and distinguish CLD_EXITED status1 from CLD_KILLED signal1. Validate new session/group identity before group signals. Hold the unreaped leader until the final group operation. ECHILD or identity loss is failure, never completion and never permission to signal a reusable numeric group.

At cleanup entry freeze TERM, KILL and direct-reap phase ends once, each at most5 seconds and within the existing overall cleanup allowance. They may not slide on retries. Normal leader exit still cleans surviving same-group work. Only the exact WNOWAIT-confirmed terminal leader is exempt from the sampled group scan; all other matching entries, including Z, prevent completion until absent. Do not reap unrelated descendants or introduce a global subreaper. Never signal this numeric group after direct reap, including error recovery.

Each /proc scan streams entries, admits at most20000 visits and20000 numeric stat reads per scan, additionally limited by the shared account remaining metadata allowance across all scans, limits each stat to8192 bytes plus one overflow-detection byte, and checks the fixed phase wall end between operations. Reserve visits and possible reads before effects against the same account; debit actual bytes and unsuccessful admitted work conservatively. Parse the parenthesized comm safely and discard it. Retain only matching pid/state/pgrp/session/starttime; do not retain other process contents. Unavailable, malformed, incomplete, overflow or over-budget scans refuse cleanup credit. This is sampled group cleanup, not detached-task detection, exhaustive thread observation or atomic containment.

After the final group check, reap only the direct child with bounded nonblocking waitpid; compare the real status to preserved waitid. Keep each failed cleanup incomplete and restore the handler even when cleanup itself fails. Parent SIGKILL or host teardown remains unverified.

## Streams and admission

Drain both nonblocking pipes during bounded waits; never let a full pipe defer clock checks indefinitely. Each stream is at most8MiB; all rows together retain/read at most16MiB. Read at most64KiB per operation, limited further by remaining stream and account budget plus one already-admitted overrun byte. Before each read reserve its maximum work. Actual returned bytes debit read_bytes, stream_bytes and spent_bytes; retained bytes additionally debit spent_bytes and retained_stream_bytes. Scan all supplied secrets and the existing fixed sensitive-pattern family before retaining/returning. Scan work also debits spent_bytes for each performed pass. Refuse a match without raw bytes in last_direct. Reserve1MiB closure within the existing256MiB new pool. No growth, cap argument or reset. Proc data shares this pool; it does not count as stdout or report retention. Never return more than the fixed retention limits, even on failure.
